digest.component_or_area: lock management and compaction sweep labeling
propositions: A blocked session cannot determine what operation holds the store write lock or whether interrupting it is safe, requiring manual identification via lsof/ps.
Compaction sweeps hold the store write lock for extended periods (24+ minutes) at low CPU utilization, blocking transactional writes with timeouts that name only a bare pid.
The sweep operation is safely interruptible without data loss because skipped sweeps are no-ops and the next trigger re-folds events, but this guarantee is not communicated to operators.
Lock holder information must reach the timeout error message ambiently through a contextvars-based operation label mechanism without modifying acquisition call sites in compact_txn.py.
The v2 lock stamp format must remain colon-free for forward compatibility while carrying an optional sanitized op= field that describes the holding operation and its safety implications.
